{"self_assessment": "Impact: I built the belly (stroke 2), the full lower half of the fish outline, which is roughly half of the body the judge sees. The belly runs from the nose to the lower notch and carries the fall on into the bottom tail. About 105 of the 120 standing dominoes were connected to the start, so the fish body reads clearly as a big fish facing left.

Execution: I laid the belly steadily in small batches from the start until it reached the lower notch. I then inspected the handover into the bottom tail and confirmed it was dark. I also worked at the right edge, extending and nudging dominoes and inspecting the area several times to check the connection to the top tail.

Collaboration: I gave the table regular progress updates, such as how many dominoes remained to the lower notch, so Jack could start the bottom tail the moment the belly landed. I suggested that the back come in wide and sweep up into the tail. When Sofia asked for space at the tail edge, I stayed hands-off so we didn't bump each other. I joined the hands-off call before the push.

Leadership: I kept the mood light and the table energised. I called out handoffs clearly and told people when to jump in. I also pointed out the right-edge issue early so others could weigh in on it. I helped the team settle on a clean, recognisable fish and finish with everyone's hands off before the push.", "my_share_percent": 30}
